title: Introduction to Capstone Projects
summary: Explains what the course's capstone projects are and how they differ from the guided projects: you get a client-style spec and an example site, but no starter files, walkthrough or solution, and the result should be original enough to go in a portfolio.

concepts.heading: Key takeaways
points: Employers judge developers mainly on what they have built, so a portfolio of real projects matters more than a list of courses.
GitHub is where the portfolio starts: you can pin chosen repositories on your profile, and the contribution graph shows how regularly you push code.
Each capstone is scoped to the skills taught so far, but expect to get stuck and to look things up in docs or online. That struggle is intended.
Capstones work like a client brief: a written specification plus an example site showing the target. No starter code, no solution files, no walkthrough video.
Do not clone the example site. Projects that are obviously copied from a popular tutorial are easy for reviewers to spot; build your own version with your own content and design choices.
The aim is to break out of relying on tutorials and to see your own progress from the first capstone to the later ones.
Capstones are optional if you are not aiming for a developer job. Share finished work in the Q&A.

pitfalls: Copying the example capstone site or tutorial code into a portfolio.
Skipping the struggle by searching for a finished solution instead of working from the spec and documentation.
